item.title: Economies Thrive With Older, Smaller Population, New Study Finds
item.description: Declining birth rates around the world have gotten many people worried about the economic impact, with predictions of slower growth and less innovation. But a new paper finds that the opposite may be true.

item.title: Ardian’s Santé Cie Seeks to Enter French Restructuring Procedure
item.description: Santé Cie SAS is seeking to enter French restructuring proceedings after some of its cash assets were seized as part of an investigation from the authorities into alleged corruption and money laundering.

item.title: Sports-Related Deals on the Rise, Says William Blair’s IB Head
item.description: Acquisitions in the sports industry are set to increase as investors leverage a slew of different approaches to the fast-growing sector, according to William Blair & Co.’s head of investment banking.

item.title: Tepper’s Appaloosa Soars 32% in First Half on Memory-Chip Makers
item.description: David Tepper’s Appaloosa Management returned 32% in the first half of the year, fueled by bets on the high-flying memory-chip sector.

item.title: Dental Chain Owner Aspen Drops WellNow Sale as Lenders Lawyer Up
item.description: The Aspen Group has indicated it’s no longer moving ahead with a planned sale of its urgent care clinic chain WellNow, after seeking buyers amid an effort to address a looming debt deadline that’s also prompted its lenders to retain lawyers.

item.title: The Restaurant Economy Doesn’t Look K-Shaped
item.description: It looks like a broad based boom.

item.title: Boston Airport Borrows $812 Million for Revamp as Traffic Soars
item.description: The busiest airport in New England is tapping the municipal bond market to remodel its facilities and keep up with passenger growth.

item.title: WEF Founder Schwab Claims He Found Spying Device at His Home
item.description: World Economic Forum founder Klaus Schwab has filed a criminal complaint following the alleged discovery of a secret listening device planted in his home office in Geneva.

item.title: Trans Mountain 3.0 Revives Indigenous Pipeline Ownership Push
item.description: Canada’s announcement last week that Trans Mountain Corp. will build a 1 million-barrel-a-day oil pipeline along the government-owned company’s existing Alberta-to-British Columbia route is rekindling Indigenous interest in acquiring a stake in the company.

item.title: Argentina Shuns Markets for Now, Sees Investment Grade by 2031
item.description: President Javier Milei’s administration is targeting investment-grade status for Argentina by the end of a potential second term in 2031, while continuing to shun international debt markets.

item.title: Hedge Fund Veterans Are Accelerating a Major Shift in Development Finance
item.description: A group of hedge fund veterans is helping drive a fundamental shift in how to generate financing for developing nations.

item.title: Germany to Sweeten Terms of Gas Plant Auction to Draw More Bids
item.description: Germany will lift the maximum amount it will pay developers in upcoming auctions for gas-fired power plants as it seeks to attract more bids for urgently needed back-up power capacity.

item.title: Bank of Canada Surveys Show War Boosted Inflation Expectations, Investment
item.description: The war in Iran caused a spike in Canadian inflation expectations and is leading the country’s oil producers to boost their investment and production plans.

item.title: Peace Deal Doesn’t Restore Pre-War Situation, ECB’s Schnabel Says
item.description: Peace efforts in the Middle East have helped bring energy prices down rapidly but haven’t restored the position the world was in before hostilities erupted, according to European Central Bank Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel.

item.title: Ontario, Alberta Pitch Cross-Canada Oil Pipeline to Ease US Reliance
item.description: Alberta and Ontario proposed a crude oil pipeline and energy corridor across Canada as a way of reducing the country’s dependence on the US.

item.title: Fed’s Waller Says ‘Forward Guidance’ Needs to Be Flexible
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said signals from policymakers on the future path of interest rates can play a useful role if done carefully.

item.title: Welltower Seeks at Least $492 Million From Canada Bond Sale
item.description: Welltower Inc. is looking to raise at least C$700 million ($492 million) in a two-part bond deal, the latest US firm to tap investors north of the border.

item.title: US Service Sector Expands at a Slower Pace, Hiring Picks Up
item.description: The US service sector expanded in June at a slightly slower pace, but firms boosted payrolls as cost pressures eased.

item.title: Microsoft’s Xbox to Cut 3,200 Jobs, Divest Five Studios in Major Overhaul
item.description: Compulsion and Double Fine studios will become independent; Undead Labs and Ninja Theory will be sold. Xbox will also look to sell or spin out Arkane Studios.

item.title: HSBC’s Kettner Sees Hyperscalers Back in Favor Amid ‘Melt-Up’
item.description: Investors who recently scorned so-called hyperscalers are starting to come back as the companies show they can mint profits while spending hundreds of billions of dollars on artificial-intelligence infrastructure, according to Max Kettner of HSBC Holdings Plc.

item.title: Israel Cuts Interest Rates to the Lowest Level Since 2022
item.description: Israel cut interest rates for a second straight meeting, to the lowest level since late 2022, with a strong currency and moderate inflation expectations outweighing an anticipated pickup in growth.

item.title: BlackRock, Vanguard ETFs Diverge Over 170% AI-Fueled Rally
item.description: For more than a decade, investors could treat the two biggest emerging-market exchange-traded funds as almost interchangeable.

item.title: Container Carriers Eye Return to Red Sea Route
item.description: A.P. Moller-Maersk A/S and Hapag-Lloyd AG signaled confidence about resuming passage through the Red Sea, sending the container carriers’ shares down on expectation a return to the shorter route will ease capacity constraints and temper a surge in shipping rates.

item.title: Lockheed to Buy Ultra Maritime for $3.45 Billion in Sea Push
item.description: Lockheed Martin Corp. agreed to buy naval defense business Ultra Maritime, which focuses on submarine detection systems, for $3.45 billion as the US defense giant broadens its undersea weapons portfolio.

item.title: Broadcom, Apple Extend Tie-Up to 2031 With New Custom Chips
item.description: Broadcom Inc. said that it will provide new custom chips to Apple Inc. in an expanded partnership that now runs through 2031.

item.title: Saudis Slash Main Oil Price to Rare Discount as Market Dives
item.description: Saudi Arabia made big reductions to its main crude oil prices for buyers in Asia, selling barrels at a discount for the first time since it embarked on a price war in 2020, as a surge of global supply heightens competition to find buyers.

item.title: Rogers Pays $3.1 Billion for Full Control of NBA, NHL Teams
item.description: Rogers Communications Inc. agreed to buy the remaining 25% stake in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment Ltd. for C$4.35 billion ($3.1 billion) from billionaire Larry Tanenbaum’s Kilmer Group, taking full ownership of Canada’s largest sports empire.

item.title: Russia Oil Price Falls to Pre-Iran War Level in Blow to Kremlin
item.description: Russia’s flagship crude price has slid to levels seen before the conflict in the Middle East, piling more pressure on Kremlin coffers that are already strained by the invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Return of the Right Sparks Record Inflow to Chile Peso Bonds
item.description: Foreign investors are piling into Chile’s local government debt at the fastest pace on record, attracted by a weaker peso, the prospect of interest rate cuts and the return of a more market-friendly government.

item.title: Europe’s Equity Bankers Bet on Capex Wave to Ride Out IPO Slump
item.description: Record spending on AI infrastructure and power grids is fueling a flurry of capital raises by listed companies, giving bankers one of their busiest starts in years and eclipsing the slowdown of initial public offerings in the region.
